title: The experiment service answers a fixed kimi-k3 request under two served identities, so provider qualification fails intermittently on every host
target: host-independent; observed from gfx938 and cross-checked against sm_103a evidence
executor_revision: none: the run never reached a device

observation:
The same request reaches two different served identities. On 2026-09-16 every assistant message in the B300 transcripts read kimi-k3 and both qualifications passed. On 2026-09-17 a request that declared kimi-k3 was answered by messages reading kimi-k3-fireworks, and the gate refused the run. Two one-turn probes minutes later, from the same host through the same proxy: asking for kimi-k3 produced three consistent kimi-k3 messages, and asking for kimi-k3-fireworks by name was not served. So this is not a rename and not a host difference -- the endpoint routes one requested name across backends and labels the message with whichever one answered.

The refusal is correct and should not be widened. S5 fixes the model so a difference is attributable to the environment rather than to model capability, and a transcript whose messages disagree with the model that was asked for cannot support that. What the gate compares is agreement inside one transcript, not agreement with the Study, so declaring the other name in the Study would not satisfy it and asking for the other name does not work anyway.

The consequence is a cost, not a compromise: campaigns now fail at qualification at whatever rate the endpoint routes elsewhere, on every host, and a retry is the only remedy the harness has. Worth stating for the earlier evidence too -- the nineteen B300 campaigns did not silently mix backends, because a mixed transcript is exactly what this gate refuses. It failed them shut rather than open.
proposed_change: Nothing in the Compiler or the Lab. Two things outside it: ask the service operator whether kimi-k3-fireworks is the same weights behind a second serving backend or a different model, because the answer decides whether a retried run is comparable to the 2026-09-16 campaigns at all; and record the observed served identity in the campaign's own record so a reader is not left inferring it from a transcript. If the rate is high enough to stall a sweep, a bounded qualification retry belongs in the launcher, where it can be counted and reported -- never in the parser, which is the thing keeping the two apart.
